ranked_evidence.title: Groundworks firm fined after seatbelt-less driver breaks ankle - Construction News
ranked_evidence.snippet: A court has fined a groundworks company £20,000 after a dumper-truck driver who had been told not to wear a seatbelt broke his ankle and foot when the vehicle overturned. Cheshire-based Jim Yates & Sons Ltd was also ordered to pay £4,824 in costs at a hearing at Warrington Magistrates’ Court on 14 July, according to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE). It said a 27-year-old man was reversing a one-tonne truck without wearing a seatbelt, in contrast with HSE guidance and the vehicle manufacturer’s instructions. The driver was thrown from the vehicle and sustained crushing injuries to his leg, resulting in a broken foot and ankle. The HSE said its investigators found Jim Yates & Sons had instructed workers not to wear seatbelts while operating one-tonne dumper trucks. Suitable protection should have been in place to stop vehicles entering the excavation, and operators should never be instructed not to wear a seatbelt.

ranked_evidence.snippet: # Conor McGregor reveals full extent of his UFC knee injury: ‘Quite shocking’. Conor McGregor has finally revealed the full extent of the knee injury that abruptly ended his long-awaited UFC comeback. McGregor said what many initially feared, confirming he tore both his ACL and meniscus during his loss to Max Holloway at UFC 329 in Las Vegas on July 11. “It is the same injury as the first Holloway fight, only this time the opposite leg. “I wonder was I saved from something worse here. The injury occurred just seconds into McGregor’s first fight in five years, where he unleashed a jumping switch kick almost immediately, blowing out his right knee in the process. Since then, he has suffered two losses to Dustin Poirier, missed years recovering from a broken leg, withdrew from a scheduled bout against Michael Chandler with a broken toe, served an 18-month suspension from the UFC after failing to disclose his whereabouts for drug testing, and now finds himself facing another lengthy rehab process following the Holloway defeat.

ranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize Cockroach Janata Party activist on hunger strike - Los Angeles Times
ranked_evidence.snippet: * Police in New Delhi forcibly moved education reform activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s Cockroach Janata Party movement for education reform. Delhi police said that Wangchuk was taken to the hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. The Cockroach Janata Party — a play on the name of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party — said in a social media post that the government “forcefully abducted” Wangchuk “without his or his family’s consent” two days before their planned march to India’s Parliament.

ranked_evidence.snippet: # Indian police forcibly hospitalize a prominent Cockroach Party activist on hunger strike. Police said activist Sonam Wangchuk was taken to hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike, and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party movement for education reform. Authorities tightened security around New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, a designated public protest ground enclosed by police barricades, where activist Sonam Wangchuk has been camped along with students and Cockroach Party activists who demand the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, after allegations that exam papers were leaked in advance. Delhi Police said Wangchuk was taken to hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike, and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move.
